prompts.prompt: We want to send docs/design/notify.md to design review on Thursday. Is it ready? Run the quality gate on it and write the result to quality-notify.md. Do not edit the design doc. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill defines a 1-5 score with fixed rules (3+ IMPORTANT plus a missing section scores 1), typed issues (missing_section, unsupported_claims, circular_reasoning, yagni_violation), and a pitfall that accurate ranges like '100-500ms' are not hedges. Without it, a reviewer gives a soft 'needs work' verdict, may miss that the missing ADR section is structural, and often flags the cold-start range.

rubric.criterion: The IMPORTANT issues in the KEY
rubric.pass: Finds all of: no ADR section despite Kafka/SPI/rules-engine decisions, YAGNI (transport SPI for SMS/push/fax, rules engine + DSL), circular Kafka justification, unsupported 20ms/45% claims
Score 1/5 with the rule applied (3+ IMPORTANT and a missing section), 'Issues: N IMPORTANT, N SUGGESTION' line, each issue with section, type, and suggestion; states it does not meet the >=3 gate
rubric.partial: Right score but format or gate statement missing

rubric.pass: Does not flag 'Lambda cold starts typically add 100-500ms' as a hedge; no invented issues
rubric.partial: Mentions the range neutrally but lists it as a minor issue
rubric.fail: Flags the range as a hedge or unsupported claim, or invents issues

rubric.pass: Each IMPORTANT issue has a concrete fix (add ADR for Kafka vs existing stream, cut SPI/DSL to email-only, cite a measurement or remove the 20ms/45% figures)

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the ready/not-ready verdict right and justified?
Did it catch the YAGNI and missing ADR?
False positives on the accurate range

prompts.prompt: Give docs/design/clean.md an objective review-readiness score and write it to quality-clean.md. The author is junior and anxious about it, so be fair and do not pad the list. Do not rewrite the doc. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill says not to penalize brevity, that qualitative rationale needs no evidence URL, and that a sourced claim is not unsupported. A competent reviewer without those rules tends to manufacture findings (asks for more sections, more detail, citations for qualitative choices) and lands at 3/5.

rubric.pass: Zero or at most a couple of SUGGESTION items, each real; the $310 claim recognized as sourced (billing report, March 2026)
rubric.partial: One debatable IMPORTANT item, or the sourced claim questioned
rubric.fail: Several invented issues or brevity penalized

rubric.criterion: Uses the skill's score and format
rubric.pass: Score line, issue-count line in the skill's format, review-ready gate stated
rubric.partial: Score present but format or gate missing

rubric.pass: Notes all required sections present, ADR with a quantified trade-off, simplest option chosen for stated requirements

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Fairness to a good, short doc

prompts.prompt: Check docs/design/minor.md for filler language and anything else that should hold it back from design review. Write a scored result to quality-minor.md. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: Under the skill's rubric, more than three SUGGESTION issues and no IMPORTANT issues scores 3/5, which still clears the >=3 gate. The doc has five filler/hedge phrases and a measured 41-second claim. Without the skill, reviewers tend to call the measured claim unsupported, or to block the doc over style issues.

rubric.pass: Quotes at least four of: Needless to say, It should be noted that, As mentioned above, In order to, somewhat; typed filler_phrases/hedge_words as SUGGESTION
The 41-second figure (measured on the March 2026 table) is not flagged as unsupported_claims; no IMPORTANT issues invented
rubric.partial: Mentions it as a possible concern but does not count it
rubric.fail: Flags it as unsupported or invents an IMPORTANT issue

rubric.pass: States the doc can advance (score 3 meets the >=3 gate) with revision notes
rubric.partial: Score right but the gate consequence unstated

rubric.pass: Each filler phrase has a rewrite or 'delete'

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Is the doc correctly allowed to advance?
